fact: Red pandas use their long, bushy tails for balance and to help keep warm.
A red fox can hear tiny animals moving beneath the ground.
Young deer have white spots that help them blend into the forest.
Raccoons have very sensitive front paws that help them explore their surroundings.
An owl can turn its head as much as about 270 degrees.
A squirrel’s front teeth never stop growing.
A hedgehog can curl into a tight ball when it feels threatened.
A rabbit’s large ears help it hear danger and keep cool.
Black bears are very good tree climbers.
Beavers have strong orange-colored teeth that are perfect for cutting wood.
Lions often live together in family groups called prides.
An elephant uses its trunk to breathe, smell, drink, and pick things up.
A giraffe has seven neck bones—the same number as a human.
Every zebra has its own unique stripe pattern.
The cheetah is the fastest land animal in the world.
Hippos spend much of the day in water to help keep cool.
A rhino’s horn is made mostly from keratin, the same material found in our fingernails.
Meerkats take turns watching for danger while the rest of the group searches for food.
The ostrich is the largest living bird in the world.
Gazelles can run quickly and make high, springy leaps.
Every tiger has its own unique pattern of stripes.
Gorillas usually move around on all fours using their knuckles.
Orangutans build leafy nests in trees where they can rest and sleep.
Tiny plants called algae can sometimes grow on a sloth’s fur.
A toucan’s large bill helps it reach fruit growing on branches.
Macaws have strong curved beaks that can crack nuts and seeds.
Jaguars are powerful swimmers as well as excellent hunters on land.
Crocodiles can grow new teeth to replace ones they lose.
Many tree frogs have sticky toe pads that help them climb.
A chameleon can move each eye in a different direction.
A cow’s stomach has four compartments that help digest tough plants.
Horses can sleep either standing up or lying down.
Pigs have an excellent sense of smell.
Sheep have unusual rectangular pupils that give them a very wide view.
Goats are excellent climbers and can balance on very steep ground.
Chickens take dust baths to help keep their feathers clean.
Ducks spread natural oil over their feathers to help keep them waterproof.
A donkey’s large ears help it hear well and release body heat.
Llamas communicate using sounds, body movements, and the position of their ears.
Alpacas often make a gentle humming sound to communicate.
Dolphins use echolocation to help them find objects underwater.
Green sea turtles travel long distances through the ocean.
An octopus has three hearts.
Male humpback whales can sing long and complicated songs.
A shark’s skeleton is made from cartilage instead of bone.
Male seahorses carry developing babies inside a special pouch.
A seal’s whiskers can detect tiny movements in the water.
Penguins use their wing-shaped flippers to swim through the water.
Many crabs can regrow a lost leg after they molt.
Clownfish can safely live among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones.
Polar bears have black skin underneath their thick fur.
Many Arctic foxes grow a white winter coat that helps them blend into the snow.
Both male and female reindeer can grow antlers.
A snow leopard’s long tail helps it balance and can wrap around its body for warmth.
Giant pandas spend many hours every day eating bamboo.
A camel’s hump stores fat, not water.
A fennec fox’s enormous ears help it stay cool in the desert.
A baby kangaroo is called a joey and grows inside its mother’s pouch.
Koalas sleep for many hours because their leafy diet provides little energy.
Mountain goats have special hooves that help them grip steep rocky slopes.
